title: Index build on large collection without monitoring — replication lag risk
expected_feedback: Standard: index build on 30M documents with nothing watching replication lag. On the supported majors the default build is REPLICATED -- every data-bearing member builds concurrently -- so the I/O lands on the secondaries too and they can fall behind. Lagging secondaries return stale reads and can enter RECOVERING. Watch it with rs.printSecondaryReplicationInfo() (NOT rs.printReplicationInfo(), which reports the connected member's oplog window) and db.currentOp() for build progress. A rolling build is NOT the remedy for lag: it removes each member from the set in turn -- shut down, restart standalone on a different port, build, restore, wait for catch-up -- costing a voting member for the whole window and taking longer. Reserve it for measured CPU or WiredTiger cache pressure. Throttle or reschedule the build instead.
violated_rule: Index builds monitored for replication lag
